extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, stakeholders, and practitioners who may submit comments on the Fish and Wildlife Service rulemaking for the scarlet macaw SPR analysis (e.g., conservation organizations, scientists, legal practitioners, interested citizens)
extracted.subtask_short: rulemaking public comment on SPR analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and standards for submitting public comments to the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service about how CBD v. Everson and the plain language of the Endangered Species Act may affect the Service's Significant Portion of the Range (SPR) analysis for the northern DPS of the southern subspecies of scarlet macaw. Includes scope of requested input, submission methods, deadlines, public posting and timelines for agency action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of solicited comments
rubrics_metrics.description: We invite written comments on the manner in which the plain language of the Act and CBD v. Everson decision may affect our February 26, 2019, final rule designating the northern DPS of the southern subspecies of scarlet macaw (A. m. macao) as a threatened species. Specifically, we are interested in public input on whether and how the CBD v. Everson opinion affects the SPR analysis in the threatened determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We request comments from any interested party that pertain to the issues raised in the preceding paragraph only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission methods and docket identification
rubrics_metrics.description: You may submit comments by one of the following methods: (1) Electronically: Go to the Federal eRulemaking Portal: https://www.regulations.gov. In the Search box, enter FWS-HQ-ES-2022-0134, which is the docket number for this rulemaking. Then, click on the Search button. You may submit a comment by clicking on 'Comment.' (2) By hard copy: Submit by U.S. mail to: Public Comments Processing, Attn: FWS-HQ-ES-2022-0134, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, MS: PRB/3W, 5275 Leesburg Pike, Falls Church, VA 22041-3803.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency requests that you send comments only by the methods described above; using the docket number on regs.gov ensures proper filing and linking to the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment deadline and electronic receipt rules
rubrics_metrics.description: We will accept comments received or postmarked on or before December 2, 2022. Comments submitted electronically using the Federal eRulemaking Portal must be received by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on the closing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hardcopy comments must be postmarked by the closing date; electronic uploads must be received by the stated time to be considered timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability and confidentiality of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit a comment via https://www.regulations.gov, your entire comment—including any personal identifying information—will be posted on the website. If you submit a hardcopy comment that includes personal identifying information, you may request that we withhold this information from public review, but we cannot guarantee that we will be able to do so. We will post all hardcopy comments on https://www.regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies review all submissions and may choose to redact, or withhold, certain submissions (or portions thereof). Submitted comments may not be available to be read until the agency has approved them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket access and supporting materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments and materials we receive will be available for public inspection at https://www.regulations.gov. The docket includes supporting documents such as 'Literature Cited Scarlet Macaw Final SPR Analysis' and other related documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the regulations.gov docket to view submitted comments and supporting literature; related documents are displayed using the agency docketing for context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency timeline for SPR reexamination and subsequent actions
rubrics_metrics.description: We will reconsider our SPR analysis based on the plain language of the Act and the implications of CBD v. Everson, and submit our findings to the Federal Register by March 28, 2023. If the SPR analysis determines that there are no significant portions of the range, the SPR analysis ends the process. If the SPR analysis determines that one or more significant portions of the range exist but do not warrant endangered status, the SPR analysis ends the process. However, if the SPR analysis finds one or more significant portions of the range and finds the northern DPS of the southern subspecies of scarlet macaw should be listed as endangered instead of threatened, we will submit a proposed rule to the Federal Register by March 28, 2024, seeking public comment on the proposed reclassification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Throughout this process, the February 26, 2019, final rule (84 FR 6278) remains in effect, including with respect to the threatened listing and section 4(d) rule for the northern DPS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal basis and case-law consideration for analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: This Action reexamines the SPR analysis in light of Center for Biological Diversity v. Everson, which vacated the Services' joint July 1, 2014 policy interpreting 'significant portion of its range', and directs reconsideration consistent with the plain language of the Endangered Species Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SPR reanalysis should be informed by the plain language of the Act and the implications of CBD v. Everson as described in the notice; comments should focus on those legal/analytical implications.

rubrics_metrics.description: This site displays a prototype of a 'Web 2.0' version of the daily Federal Register. It is not an official legal edition of the Federal Register, and does not replace the official print version or the official electronic version on GPO's govinfo.gov. rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those relying on the content for legal research should verify against the official edition (PDF on govinfo.gov); only official editions provide legal notice and judicial notice under 44 U.S.C. 1503 & 1507.
